### 📓 Docs Drift Check
⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files. Nothing else in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **1** changed package(s)).

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 14c67d446e577926460f3ed893e44cc32cbecb12` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6943445b89f637352585ead984a2fd63d4e4fe37`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts + packages/spec/scripts/conversions-major18-merge.test.ts (the gate that enforces the rule), packages/spec/src/conversions/entries/18/*.ts (the 95 modules the docblock describes), .claude/skills/spec-property-retirement/SKILL.md on `main` after PR #30109 (the same steps, read for agreement), AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3, scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs, packages/spec/package.json `files[]` and packages/spec/tsup.config.ts (read for ②)

Inputs: card #29994 (body; comments 6619509152, 6619532361, 6632322266, 6634099014, 6666793161, 6668036951), PR #30643 (body, file list, net diff against `main` at `778aedf666`), the check-runs on the head read at 2026-11-05T20:14Z: 23 completed success (among them `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Plan Test Core shards`, every `Lint ·` lane, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`), 14 skipped by path filter, 0 failed; 29 still in progress at read time (`Build Core`, `Test Core` 1–8 — which carry `conversions-major18-merge.test.ts` — `Test UI` 1–16, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`). This verdict reads the completed conclusions; a later failure among the in-progress runs is a new fact for the queue, not covered here

### ① Derived judgments

- No code line of `registry.ts` changed — right. The net diff is 9+/5− lines and every changed line is a ` * ` line inside the one block comment that opens at L160 and closes at L189 on `main` (L193 on the head); nothing outside that comment is touched, so the comment-stripped bytes of the file equal `main`'s. The imports (L24–135), `OrderedConversion` (L146–151), `inApplicationOrder` (L154–158), the 95 entries of `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS` (L194–296), `CONVERSIONS_BY_MAJOR` (L326–349) and `ALL_CONVERSIONS` (L355–358) are byte-identical to `main`.
- Public surface: none — right. `MAJOR_18_CONVERSIONS` is a non-exported const; the exported `CONVERSIONS_BY_MAJOR` and `ALL_CONVERSIONS` and their docblocks are unchanged, so `dist/*.d.ts`, `api-surface` and every schema-derived generated artifact are unaffected.
- Accept-set: unchanged — right. The docblock now states the rule `conversions-major18-merge.test.ts` already enforces (④); the test, the `PLACED_BEFORE_THE_RULE` exemption (46 names) and every other gate are untouched, so nothing becomes accepted or refused that was not before.
- `Fixes #29994` — right. The card's two deliverables are the SKILL.md steps (landed in PR #30109, partial landing 6634099014) and this docblock (scope addition 6619532361); this PR closes the remainder.

### ② Semver level

- `skip-changeset` (label on the PR; `Check Changeset` success) — right. AGENTS.md step 3 reserves the label for "a diff that publishes nothing from any released package". `@objectstack/spec`'s `files[]` are `dist`, `json-schema`, `liveness`, `prompts`, `llms.txt`, `README.md`, `src/**/*.zod.ts`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `api-surface`, `spec-changes.json`, `protocol-upgrade-guide.md`. `registry.ts` is not a `*.zod.ts`; the docblock sits on a non-exported const, so no `.d.ts` carries it; `tsup.config.ts` sets no `legalComments`, so esbuild drops a `/** */` block that carries no `@license`/`@preserve` (the file's `@__PURE__` annotations are not in the hunk); the sourcemaps ship without `sourcesContent` (`check:sourcemap-no-sources-content`). The changed text reaches no published artifact, so there is nothing a changeset could describe.
- `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs`: no `.changeset/*.md` is added, modified or deleted — both of its rules are vacuous here; green.
- `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none` — right: nothing an author can write, and no export, changes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag (PR body; report 6668036951): the test anchors a last-sorting import after the last `./entries/18/` import, not on `OrderedConversion`. Confirmed. `definitionsTail` (test L149–154) returns the line after the last `DEFINITION` match (L62, which recognises `./entries/18/ID.js` imports only), and `placementFindings` (L170–186) demands that the last entry's import have no `./entries/18/` import after it (the `want === undefined` arm, L182–183). `OrderedConversion` appears nowhere in the test. Today the last such import (L135) is also the last import of the file, two lines above `OrderedConversion`'s docblock (L137), so both anchors coincide; the new sentence names the one the test reads. Answered.
- `open_questions: []` — none.
- Dev deviations (the attribution HTML comment as the PR body's first line; the dispatch prompt's two-line footer): PR-body form only; `PR-body guards` success. Accepted.
- Docs Drift Check comment 6668037579 ("1 changed file yielded no anchor"): a comment-only hunk in a file no docs page anchors; `Flag docs affected by code changes` success. No action.
- The seat claim's ⛔ list (6666793161: no code line of `registry.ts`, no edit to the merge test, no `.claude/**`) held — the file list is `registry.ts` alone and ① shows no code line moved.
- Triage 6619509152 ("no `@objectstack/skills` changeset applies") covered the skill half; the spec half is judged in ②.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts` L181–189, read against `packages/spec/scripts/conversions-major18-merge.test.ts` on `main` (unchanged since PR #29993's split, `d79eecfe5b`), the 95 modules under `src/conversions/entries/18/`, and SKILL.md on `main` (`28ce3d1bfa`).

Each sentence against what enforces it:
- "DEFINE it in a module of its own, `./entries/18/ID.ts`, the file named for the conversion's `id`" — `definitionsOf` (L144–146) takes the id from the import path, `MODULE_PATH` (L64) resolves `entries/18/${id}.ts`, and `definitionInModule` (L157–161) requires `id: 'ID'` inside that file: the file name IS the id, and the test refuses any other. 95/95 modules on `main` have that shape (`const IDENT: MetadataConversion = {`, an `id:` equal to the file name, `export { IDENT };` as the last line).
- "exporting it by name (`export { IDENTIFIER };`)" — `definitionInModule` requires the module to end with exactly that statement; the form the docblock prints is the form the test accepts.
- "A new file never conflicts" — test header L26–27; git conflicts only on edits to one path.
- "IMPORT it directly above the import of the entry that follows it in this list, so the conversion imported next after it is that entry" — `placementFindings` L174–185: for a non-exempt entry at list index i, the next `./entries/18/` import after its own must be the entry at i+1. `definitionSite` (L204–210), which builds the accepted retirement, inserts at `docStart` of the successor's import — the same instruction. Walked by hand: a conversion sorting first (successor `actionAriaRemoved`, import L119); one between two exempt neighbours; one between a rule-placed predecessor and that predecessor's successor (the predecessor's next import becomes the new one, which is now the entry that follows it — the test's own neighbour case, L404–413); two successive last-sorting ones (the second goes after the first, which then precedes it in the list too). All accepted.
- "One that sorts last is imported after every other `./entries/18/` import" — `definitionsTail` L149–154 and the `want === undefined` arm of L182–183. Holds (③).
- "The imports stand where the definitions stood before the split" — the file's codemod note L20–23 and the test header L29–31.
- "their end is one gap too: importing every new conversion there conflicts exactly as appending here did" — the lit control L442–446 (`definitions-end-a` × `definitions-end-b` must conflict) built by `retireAtDefinitionsEnd` L232–235.
- The unchanged bullets still match: insert where the identifier sorts (`sortFindings` L164–167, the list-end control L436–440); `order` one more than the highest (`NEXT_ORDER` L313); equal `order` applies in `id` order (`inApplicationOrder` L154–158, `applicationOrder` L238–244, asserted L426). The closing pointer to the test is true: the test holds the sort rule and the placement rule for every entry outside the exemption.

Skill agreement: SKILL.md L176–177 (`entries/TOMAJOR/ID.ts`, 文件名即 `id`, 按名 `export`; `registry.ts` 加 import 与列表项) and L215–218 (18 步: 照其头注按标识符插入 `{ conversion, order }`; import 插在后继条目的 import 正上方; 尾部追加被 merge 测试拒收) say what the docblock now says; no sentence of either contradicts the other. The skill's gloss "(头注的「定义」拆分后即 import)" explained the OLD bullet and is now redundant rather than wrong — `.claude/**`, outside this card's remaining surface; nothing owed here.

Break attempts — a literal follower of the docblock against the test:
- S1 — should-fix, `registry.ts` L181–182. The docblock names the module `./entries/18/ID.ts` and says "IMPORT it" but never says the import specifier is spelled `./entries/18/ID.js`. `DEFINITION` (test L62) recognises only `from './entries/18/ID.js'`; an import spelled `.ts` is reported by `placementFindings` as "no import of IDENT from its module in the file" (L177) and fails L335–342 — and `tsc` refuses it first (`allowImportingTsExtensions` is set only in `packages/spec/tsconfig.scripts.json`, not for `src`). The 95 neighbouring imports show the spelling, so an author who copies a neighbour is safe; one clause ("imported as `./entries/18/ID.js`") closes it for one who does not.
- S2 — should-fix, `registry.ts` L181–183. "exporting it by name" is also satisfied, in TypeScript's vocabulary, by `export const IDENTIFIER: MetadataConversion = {`, which `definitionInModule` refuses: it wants a bare `const IDENTIFIER: MetadataConversion = {` with `id` then `toMajor: 18` as the first two keys, and `export { IDENTIFIER };` as the module's final line. The parenthetical prints the accepted form, so a literal follower passes; saying the export is a separate last statement, or "as every module under `entries/18/` is written", stops the other reading before the test does.
- No sentence of the new text is false of the test or of the tree; no must-fix.
